how: Around ten clubs in Paris proper (Paris Arc Club, Inter-Activites, Arc Club Paris 12, Archers de Paris) and about 80 more in the Ile-de-France suburbs offer discovery sessions and club archery; clubs lend equipment.
The Paris Universite Club cricket section trains beginners and experienced players from age 7 at Stade Pershing in the Bois de Vincennes, with women's and junior groups.
Paris Gaels GAA (founded 1995) trains Gaelic football, hurling/camogie and handball at Stade Louis Lumiere (20e) and in Pantin, with free first trials and annual membership of about 80 EUR.
Arkose runs a dozen bouldering and rope-climbing gyms across Paris and its inner suburbs (Nation, Montmartre, Pantin, Montreuil, Saint-Denis, Nanterre), with a discovery first entry for 10 EUR.
Arkose gyms in and around Paris (e.g. Chevaleret, Issy-les-Moulineaux voie, Massy, Nation) offer roped wall climbing for all levels with a 10 EUR discovery entry.
Multiple Paris improv theatre groups run weekly shows, beginner workshops and free trial classes (Improvibes, Impro Studio, Kpten Impro), listed on Meetup.
Danse a Paris cours et soirees runs weekly Argentine tango classes and open practice (practica) on Friday evenings, listed on Meetup.
venue: Danse a Paris cours et soirees

how: English-language stand-up shows and open mics run several nights a week in Paris (Green Mic Comedy, Kuhl Comedy open mic, Dissident Club, Wokistan Comedy Club in Pantin); French-language clubs also exist.
Several Paris schools and groups run weekly salsa, bachata and kizomba classes with a free first trial class (The Paris Salsa Bachata Kizomba, Studio Jahido, Queer Salsa Dance).
Beginner piano initiation sessions and jazz-jam evenings with piano are listed on Meetup in Paris; conservatoires and private teachers provide regular lessons.
Guitar classes are listed on Meetup in Paris alongside open-mic and jam nights; private teachers and music schools offer regular lessons.
SuperSample Paris holds a weekly beatmaking and music-creation workshop, and Let's Make a Song runs paid studio sessions.
Several groups run drop-in life drawing with nude models for about 13-35 EUR a session (Life Drawing Montmartre, Paris Modele Vivant, Conservatoire de dessin et de peinture de Paris).
Drawing-from-nature workshops and bistro drawing evenings are listed on Meetup in Paris; no dedicated Urban Sketchers outing was confirmed.
venue: The Art Club (Le Bistrot des Artistes)

how: Meetup groups (Paris Hiking, Rando/Hike Ile de France, Power Hiking Paris, Plein air Paris) run weekend group hikes of 11-27 km in forests around Paris such as Rambouillet, Fontainebleau and Rougeau, many reachable by train.
Recurring Meetup photo walks (Take a Photo Walk Paris, Free Photo Walks Paris) and beginner studio workshops run across Paris.
The Wild Watercolor Workshop runs weekly beginner watercolour and drawing classes in Paris, with further watercolour ateliers listed on Meetup.
A weekly oil painting and drawing class (about 30 EUR) is run by the Meetup group Initiation a la peinture a l'huile in Paris.
venue: Initiation a la peinture a l'huile

how: Camping Indigo Paris in the Bois de Boulogne is a seven-hectare campsite with about 510 pitches for tents, caravans and camper vans.
Bercy Skatepark is a covered 800 sq m skatepark with ramps in Parc de Bercy, used by skateboarders, rollerbladers and BMXers.
Bercy Skatepark in Parc de Bercy is open to BMX riders alongside skaters and rollerbladers; dedicated BMX track clubs exist in the suburbs.
Public ice rinks include Patinoire Sonja-Henie and Espace Pailleron in Paris, plus suburban rinks at Courbevoie, Asnieres, Champigny, Vitry, Fontenay-sous-Bois and Neuilly-sur-Marne.
Multi-sport clubs Paris Universite Club (Stade Charlety, 13e) and Racing Club de France (Bois de Boulogne) run fencing sections.
Judo sections run at Paris Universite Club (Stade Charlety) and Racing Club de France, alongside many neighbourhood dojos.
Paris has Top 14 club Stade Francais (Stade Jean-Bouin, 16e) plus amateur rugby union sections at Paris Universite Club and Racing Club de France.
The Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines leisure base offers sailing and windsurfing on its lake; Lac de Creteil in the east of the metro area also lists sailing, dinghy and windsurf clubs.
venue: Base de plein air et de loisirs de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines

how: Dinghy sailing and windsurfing on the lakes of Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines and Creteil; no open-sea sailing within the metro area.
venue: Base de plein air et de loisirs de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines

how: Canoe-kayak is offered at the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines leisure base and kayak clubs operate at Lac de Creteil.
Rowing clubs are listed at Lac de Creteil, and rowboats can be rented on the Lac Inferieur in the Bois de Boulogne.
A dragon boat club is listed among the clubs at Lac de Creteil.
venue: Lac de Creteil dragon boat club

how: Riding stables operate in the Bois de Boulogne (horse and pony rides at weekends) and at the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines base, which offers riding year-round from age two.
No natural crags lie within the metro area; the sandstone boulders of the Fontainebleau forest (about 60 km southeast, roughly 1 hour by train) are the nearest outdoor climbing and bouldering.
Meetup walking groups lead forest walks in the Paris region (Rambouillet forest nature hike, Plein air Paris hikes for about 2 EUR), reachable by train.
Lekrea runs a leather craftsmanship workshop with many dates in Bastille-Popincourt, listed on Eventbrite.
A2Z Atelier runs a weekly calligraphy and Chinese painting workshop at A2Z Art Gallery in Saint-Germain-des-Pres.
Friday evening ceramic classes are listed on Eventbrite at Faubourg du Temple near Hopital Saint-Louis (10e).
La Fourche-Guy Moquet (17e) hosts creative workshops including linocut (linogravure) printmaking; screenprinting itself was not confirmed.
No track exists in the Paris region; France's only bobsleigh track is at La Plagne in the Alps, roughly 7 hours away by road or rail.
Requires alpine terrain and snow; the nearest ski jumps are in the Alps (Courchevel, Chamonix), roughly 7-8 hours from Paris.
Needs high mountain rock faces; the Paris basin is flat, and the nearest big walls are in the Alps (Chamonix area), roughly 7-8 hours away.
A desert-region tradition with no camel-racing scene in the Paris region; races are held in the Gulf states, North Africa and Australia.
A Central Asian horseback sport played in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries; no buzkashi is played in the Paris region.

Needs a tidal coast; the nearest are the Normandy bays (Mont-Saint-Michel, Baie de Somme), roughly 2.5-4 hours from Paris.
No ocean coast in the Paris region; the nearest surfable Atlantic waves are in Brittany, Vendee or the Basque coast, roughly 3-6 hours away.
Needs hills or cliffs for launch; the Paris basin is flat, and the nearest launch sites are on the Normandy cliffs or in the Alps, several hours away.
